part_title: Developer Tools and CDK: Synthesis, SAM Testing and Event-Driven Example

scenes.title: Developer Tools Working Together
scenes.narration: This opening diagram shows how AWS developer tools fit into one deployment workflow rather than treating every tool as a competitor. Start with TypeScript or Python source code and the infrastructure definitions written with CDK or SAM. Synthesis produces a CloudFormation template, which describes the desired AWS resources in JSON or YAML. CloudFormation then creates or updates resources such as Lambda, API Gateway, EC2, load balancing or a database. Look at the two supporting paths underneath. CodeArtifact supplies approved software dependencies for application builds, and the AWS CLI or SDK calls AWS APIs for deployment and operational tasks. CDK, SAM, CloudFormation, CLI and SDK all interact with AWS services through authenticated API requests, but at different abstraction levels. A useful mental model is source code defines intent, CloudFormation reconciles infrastructure, and service APIs perform the operations. In production, make source and dependency versions reproducible, review the planned changes and use a deployment role with narrowly scoped permissions. No infrastructure-as-code framework by itself makes an overprivileged workload secure.

scenes.title: CDK Mental Model and Workflow
scenes.narration: Follow the CDK hierarchy in the lower half. An App is the root of the CDK program; a Stack represents a deployable CloudFormation unit; and Constructs represent building blocks such as S3 buckets, Lambda functions or more complex reusable components. The TypeScript example creates an App and a Stack. When you run cdk synth, the code executes locally to produce a CloudFormation template describing resources and properties. This does not create the bucket or Lambda function in AWS yet. Deployment is a separate step: CDK submits the synthesised template through CloudFormation, which provisions the resources using the deploying identity's permissions. Look at the distinction between source code and generated template. TypeScript, Python and other supported languages can offer loops, classes and composition while CloudFormation remains the underlying deployment model. That also means CloudFormation limitations, replacement rules and resource policies still apply. Review the synthesised output and use consistent context, account and Region settings so the same source doesn't accidentally target a different environment.

scenes.title: CDK vs SAM: Different Abstractions, Same Foundation
scenes.narration: This comparison places AWS CDK and AWS SAM beside the same CloudFormation foundation. CDK uses programming-language abstractions and constructs to define many kinds of AWS infrastructure. It can express a multi-service architecture with reusable components and generated CloudFormation resources. SAM emphasises declarative templates with serverless-specific resources for services such as Lambda, API Gateway and DynamoDB. Both approaches ultimately work with CloudFormation deployment and its change-management semantics, even though their authoring experiences differ. The right question is how your team designs and maintains infrastructure. A team building complex VPC, container and database resources might favour CDK constructs. A small Lambda API may be simpler to describe with a focused SAM template and local tooling. These are not mutually exclusive; for example, a CDK-synthesised Lambda can be tested with compatible SAM local commands. Don't select a tool by assuming it changes IAM permission behavior or bypasses CloudFormation. Whichever abstraction you use, validate resources, review changes and apply least privilege to both deployment and application roles.

scenes.title: Test CDK Functions Locally with SAM
scenes.narration: This slide is a concrete local-testing procedure. First define the Lambda function in CDK, specifying its runtime, handler and packaged code. Run cdk synth to generate the CloudFormation template under the cdk dot out directory. Then call sam local invoke with the generated template path and the correct logical ID for the function. SAM starts a Lambda-like runtime container through Docker and passes your sample JSON event to the handler. The terminal output lets you validate parsing, function behavior and selected dependencies before deployment. A critical detail is that the CDK construct name and the generated CloudFormation logical ID are not always identical; inspect the synthesised template if the command cannot find the resource. The bottom warning is important: local execution does not fully emulate AWS IAM, S3, DynamoDB networking or other managed-service integration. A handler passing locally can still fail in AWS due to role permissions, environment variables or endpoint access. Use this workflow for fast code feedback, then test the actual deployed service with controlled integration tests.

scenes.title: Image Analysis Application Architecture
scenes.narration: Now apply those development concepts to a practical, event-driven architecture. A user uploads a research image into an S3 dataset bucket. The ObjectCreated event invokes Lambda, which calls Amazon Rekognition DetectLabels and writes the analysis result into DynamoDB. The saved record can include the object key, version, detected labels and confidence scores. Follow the permissions checklist: the Lambda execution role needs narrowly scoped S3 object reads, permission for the required Rekognition operation, DynamoDB writes to the intended table and CloudWatch logging. It does not need broad administrator access. The diagram also highlights idempotency. S3 event delivery can produce repeated processing, so use a stable identifier such as bucket, key and object version where available and design writes to avoid duplicate results. Logs, metrics and failure handling help distinguish a broken event notification from a Rekognition API or DynamoDB error. Scientific or educational workflows should treat detected labels as predictions with confidence, not verified facts. This example can be packaged and deployed using CDK or SAM and validated step by step.
